payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear explanation of how variance is calculated from model outputs through the Expected Gradient Length (EGL) method, which is linked to variance reduction in estimators.

claims.text: Expected Gradient Length (EGL) is used to compute the expected change in model parameters, which relates to reducing variance in estimators.
EGL computes the expectation of the gradient norm over the most probable labelings, which helps in variance reduction.
The method of EGL is justified from a variance reduction perspective, indicating its effectiveness in improving model outputs.
